paragraphs: Fostering for Slough Borough Council is provided by Slough Children First, which runs the local service under the name Foster with Slough. The council's own fostering page says there is an urgent need for more local foster carers and that very few things stand in the way of becoming one. The independent agencies shown above also list Slough as an area they cover, so people living in the town can compare the council's service with agencies before choosing.

Slough is also one of 20 councils in Local Authority Fostering South East, a regional fostering hub launched on 8 July 2024 as part of a Department for Education pilot. When it launched, the councils said there were more than 11,000 children in care across the South East and fewer than 3,000 foster carers approved by local authorities in the region, which is why every council in the partnership is trying to find more homes nearby.

Slough Children First says its rates from 1 April 2026 give carers a weekly allowance for each child, from £195 for a child under three to £298 for a young person aged 16 or 17, plus a weekly payment of £200, £230 or £300 depending on the carer's tier, and an extra £50 or £100 a week when a child has more complex needs. Our Slough allowance page sets out the full scale and the extras.

A good way to start is to speak to the council and two or three of the services above, and ask each about training, out-of-hours support, the support worker you would have and what they pay for the age of child you hope to care for.

sources.title: South East local authorities join forces to recruit more foster carers (Slough Borough Council, 8 July 2024)
